articles.summary:
Delhi recorded its cleanest air this month on Tuesday, with the Air Quality Index (AQI) settling at 204 in the 'poor' category, offering some respite after days of deteriorating air quality, though the relief is likely to be short-lived.
The last time the national capital recorded a lower AQI was on October 31, when the index stood at 117 in the 'moderate' category. Tuesday's reading was the lowest recorded in November, making it the least polluted day of the month so far.
The relatively better air quality on Tuesday was partly due to favourable meteorological conditions, the Air Quality Early Warning System said.
Northwesterly winds reaching speeds of up to 15 kmph and a mixing depth of around 1,500 metres helped disperse pollutants.

articles.title: Nvidia shares crash 24% amid Huang scandal. Why UBS sees 54% upside
articles.summary: Shares of Nvidia have plunged around 24% since the start of the month, wiping out more than $1 trillion in market value amid controversy surrounding CEO Jensen Huang's alleged extramarital affair with a Chinese spy and his subsequent resignation. However, UBS has sought to allay investor concerns, pointing to attractive valuations following the sharp selloff.While many analysts are sounding the alarm over Nvidia’s future, UBS thinks the assumptions are brutal and unlikely to be correct, given the chip giant's momentum for at least two more years, even without Huang as CEO, Yahoo Finance reported. In essence, the market assumes that 2028 will be the peak for Nvidia, with no growth thereafter and EBITDA margins compressing by 1,500 basis points, UBS analyst Tim Arcuri wrote on Monday. "This seems incredibly draconian to us."Nvidia valuations after selloffThe UBS analyst believes that the near-term damage to the stock has been done. He believes that it doesn't make sense to give up on the stock after being down this much especially ahead of January hyperscaler earnings calls where the international brokerage thinks capex will be guided higher than current Street expectations.UBS maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on Nvidia shares but reduced its target price to $240 apiece from $300 per share. The latest target price still implies around 54% upside potential from the stock’s previous closing price of $156.14 apiece.Also read | Nvidia board not considering Jensen Huang's return as CEO, focuses on probe: ReportBank of America analyst Vivek Arya, as quoted by the report, also feels that the stock has become sharply cheap after the selloff. He noted that 11x forward PE is a multi-decade low and a 36% forward discount to close peer Broadcom, reflecting a considerable amount of stress and potential for rebound.All eyes on Nvidia earningsNvidia is all set to announce its third-quarter earnings on Tuesday, with investors eagerly awaiting the chipmaker’s results after Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy and his subsequent resignation sparked a massive 24% plunge in the stock this month so far.The Q3 earnings print would mark the first quarterly results announcement without Huang at the helm of the chipmaker. He resigned as the CEO of the company last week, following which Nvidia's finance chief, Colette Kress, took charge as the interim CEO. Its board has said it is in the process of selecting a search firm for the CEO role.Nvidia’s earnings also come at a critical juncture in the AI trade. Earlier this year, chip linked stocks rallied sharply as hyperscalers spiked their AI spendings and new innovations related to the nascent technology came to light. However, analysts soon began to question the massive capex plans and whether they will actually bear fruits in future, leading to an equally sharp downturn in the stocks that rallied during the frenzy.Nvidia is seen as one of the faces of the artificial intelligence-led boom. articles.title: Fed's Barr flags AI risks to financial stability, warns of market disruption
articles.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr has warned that artificial intelligence could pose growing risks to financial markets, cybersecurity and consumer protection, raising concerns about the technology's potential to destabilise the financial system, according to a report by Reuters.Barr's remarks follow the US Federal Reserve's latest Financial Stability Report, released on Friday, which showed that 87% of surveyed contacts identified AI as a significant risk to the financial system. Concerns included AI-powered cyberattacks, complex financing arrangements and the possibility of a slowdown in AI-related earnings triggering a broader stock market decline.Also Read |South Korean stocks fall for fourth day as AI worries hit chipmakersAccording to Reuters, Barr on Monday highlighted additional risks, including the possibility that widespread reliance on AI-driven trading models could encourage herd behaviour and amplify market volatility. He also warned that self-learning algorithms could potentially manipulate markets and create financial instability.Barr raised concerns about the growing use of AI agents in retail banking, noting that banks could struggle to establish whether an AI system attempting to access or operate customer accounts has received proper authorisation. Even legitimate AI agents acting on behalf of customers could accelerate bank runs by moving money at unprecedented speeds, potentially overwhelming traditional safeguards, the report stated.Also Read |Chinese yuan steadies near two-week peak ahead of Xi-Trump meetingCybersecurity presents another significant challenge, with AI-enabled attackers and rogue AI agents potentially exploiting vulnerabilities across the financial system, Barr said.He also cautioned that AI developers face challenges in ensuring their models are properly controlled, legally precise, explainable and reproducible. The technology could reinforce existing biases in consumer lending and create risks of collusion, market manipulation and trading strategies capable of triggering significant volatility or systemic instability.Barr's comments, prepared for delivery in Milan, Italy, came ahead of a conference at the San Francisco Federal Reserve, where Fed Chair Kevin Warsh was scheduled to bring together AI developers, business leaders and academics to discuss the technology's implications for productivity, employment and the broader economy.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. articles.title: Net dollar purchases more than halve in October as hedging curbs support rupee
articles.summary: Mumbai: Net dollar purchases in the forwards market more than halved through October from the previous month to about $17 billion as targeted regulatory curbs on hedging took effect, building stability in the value of the rupee that surged from the end of the month to anchor a stunning revival of overseas interest in India-listed growth assets.The Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR), brought in to dissuade unnecessary currency hedging amid a haemorrhage that even record hauls from forex-inflow programmes couldn't seemingly staunch, immediately reduced dollar purchases in the forward market in October to $49 billion from $76 billion in September, CCIL data showed.135906856Dollar sales, meanwhile, reduced to $32 billion from $41 billion, marking a broader reduction in dollar demand that stood in sharp relief against a steady climb in the dollar index over the past four weeks. The dollar climbed 1.5% against a basket of six heavily traded currencies through this period, while the removal of state oil retailers' demand from the spot market and absence of unnecessary hedging provided the spot rupee the cushion it needed to draw in overseas funds.Read more: Indian equities ride global AI trade unwind: Is D-Street back on foreign investors' radar? BNP Paribas answers"Overall hedging has gone down after FERR and things have got more stringent. So, hedging happens only for what is required," said Sajal Gupta, head of forex and commodities at Nuvama. "Importers are hedging on a short-term basis while exporters still feel that the weakness in the rupee may reappear and are holding back on hedging."Read more: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on TuesdayHedging demand over the last few years has contributed to increased dollar demand, with importers hedging more and exporters hedging less.The rupee has recovered since mid-October, after touching near 97 levels last month. It closed at 93.92 on Monday, and has gained more than 3% from its record low levels.'Weakness Bias'The gap between forward dollar purchases and sales widened to $233 billion in FY26 from $97 billion in FY24, indicating a substantial increase in net dollar demand arising from hedging activity. Importers increasingly hedged amid expectations of sustained rupee deprecation, while exporters reduced their dollar sales, thus increasing dollar demand.FERR increased importer hedging costs by requiring banks to park 20% of the rupee value of eligible forward contracts with the RBI in non-interest-bearing cash reserves. This raises banks' funding and opportunity costs, which are passed on to importers through higher hedging charges, making forward dollar purchases more expensive."However, the effectiveness of FERR will depend on how long importer hedging remains curtailed. If the expectation of continued rupee depreciation persists, then importer hedging could pick up," said Gaura Sengupta, chief economist, IDFC First Bank.

Gold has fallen 31.5% since reaching a record $5,594.82 in January and is heading for its worst year since 2015.“Markets expect higher interest rates ahead, boosting the dollar and compounding gold’s headwinds, leaving it exposed to deeper declines,” Nikos Tzabouras, senior financial editorial writer at FXCM, told Reuters.For live updates on US Markets, click hereThe dollar is trading near its highest level since April 2025, making dollar-denominated bullion more expensive for buyers using other currencies and weakening demand in recent months.Treasury yields have also risen as markets price in a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate increase in December, along with a smaller probability of a 50-basis-point move, according to the CME FedWatch tool.Volatility in Nvidia shares has added to the pressure. The chipmaker’s market value fell by $1.9 trillion from early October to $3.9 trillion as of Friday, potentially prompting investors to sell gold to raise cash.“In the short term gold is a liquidity asset … the thing you sell to raise cash,” Nicky Shiels at MKS PAMP told Reuters.Middle East war fuels inflation concernsThe US-Israeli war against Iran, which began in late February, has driven oil prices higher, adding to inflation and fueling expectations of tighter monetary policy worldwide.Although non-yielding gold is traditionally viewed as a hedge against inflation, it tends to lose appeal when interest rates rise because it does not generate income.Physically backed gold exchange-traded funds attracted 211 metric tons of inflows during the third quarter despite higher bond yields and a stronger dollar. Demand for bars and coins, however, declined sharply.Also Read: Morgan Stanley turns bullish on global stocks, targets S&P 500 at 8,700Central-bank demand may weakenCentral banks remained active buyers earlier in the year, purchasing an estimated 675 tons between January and September, according to the World Gold Council.Demand from this segment could slow after Poland, the year’s most active official buyer, reached its target of 700 tons of gold reserves in November.
